statement:
Solve the system of equations (\(x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}\)):
\[\begin{cases} 6x - y + z^2 = 3 \\ x^2 - y^2 - 2z = -1 \\ 6x^2 - 3y^2 - y - 2z^2 = 0 \end{cases}\]

a) Let \((a_n)\) be defined by \(a_n = \ln(2n^2+1) - \ln(n^2+n+1)\) for all \(n \geq 1\). Prove that the set \(\{n \in \mathbb{N} \mid \{a_n\} < \tfrac{1}{2}\}\) is finite (where \(\{x\}\) denotes the fractional part).
b) Let \((b_n)\) be defined by \(b_n = \ln(2n^2+1) + \ln(n^2+n+1)\) for all \(n \geq 1\). Prove that the set \(\{n \in \mathbb{N} \mid \{b_n\} < \tfrac{1}{2016}\}\) is infinite.

Let \(ABC\) be an acute triangle with \(B, C\) fixed. Let \(D\) be the midpoint of \(BC\) and \(E, F\) the feet of perpendiculars from \(D\) to \(AB, AC\).
a) Let \(O\) be the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC\), \(M = EF \cap AO\), \(N = EF \cap BC\). Prove that the circumcircle of \(\triangle AMN\) passes through a fixed point.
b) Let \(T\) be the intersection of the tangents to the circumcircle of \(\triangle AEF\) at \(E\) and \(F\). Prove that \(T\) lies on a fixed line.

Two kinds of trees are planted on an \(m \times n\) grid (one tree per cell). A planting is called \emph{impressive} if: i) the number of trees of each kind is equal; ii) in every row and column, the counts of each kind differ by at least half the number of cells in that row/column.
a) Find an impressive planting for \(m = n = 2016\).
b) Prove that if an impressive planting exists then \(4 \mid m\) and \(4 \mid n\).

Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in circle \((O)\) with \(\angle B, \angle C\) acute. Let \(M\) be a point on arc \(BC\) not containing \(A\) such that \(AM \not\perp BC\). Line \(AM\) meets the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\) at \(T\). The circumcircle of \(\triangle AOT\) meets \((O)\) again at \(N\).
a) Prove that \(\angle BAM = \angle CAN\).
b) Let \(I\) be the incenter and \(G\) the foot of the angle bisector from \(A\). Lines \(AI, MI, NI\) meet \((O)\) again at \(D, E, F\). Let \(P = DF \cap AM\), \(Q = DE \cap AN\). The circle through \(P\) tangent to \(AD\) at \(I\) meets \(DF\) at \(H\); the circle through \(Q\) tangent to \(AD\) at \(I\) meets \(DE\) at \(K\). Prove that the circumcircle of \(\triangle GHK\) is tangent to \(BC\).

a) Prove that if \(n\) is an odd perfect number then \(n = p^s m^2\) where \(p\) is a prime of the form \(4k+1\), \(s\) is a positive integer of the form \(4h+1\), and \(m \in \mathbb{Z}^+\) is not divisible by \(p\).
b) Find all \(n \in \mathbb{Z}^+\), \(n > 1\), such that both \(n-1\) and \(\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\) are perfect numbers.
